entity: United States Department of the Interior Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
role: federal commenter on Section 4(f) / Roosevelt School property
stance_basis: defers determination of recreation significance to another authority while noting opinion aligns with Mr. Davis
summary: The United States Department of the Interior Bureau of Outdoor Recreation responded to requests regarding Section 4(f) applicability to the Roosevelt School property and the Cook County Forest Preserve District. In their November 7, 1974 letter, they deferred the determination of recreation significance to the Director of the Park District for Chicago Heights, and noted their opinion corresponded with that of Mr. Davis while clarifying it was provided only as technical assistance and did not necessarily represent the Department of the Interior's official position. They also indicated no additional response was needed regarding the Forest Preserve property given the well-documented coordination efforts.
complaint_summary: The Bureau of Outdoor Recreation responded to the Section 4(f) reapplicability inquiry regarding Roosevelt School property, deferred the determination of recreation significance to the Director of the Park District for Chicago Heights, and stated their opinion (corresponding with Mr. Davis) was provided only as technical assistance and did not represent the Department of the Interior's official position.

statement.text:
United States Department
of the Interior (BOR)
(November 7, 1974)
4(a) This is in response to your reapplicability of Section 4(f) to the Roosevelt School property, F.A. Route 23 (U.S. 30) Lincoln Highway, Cook County, Illinois. We regret the delay in our response.
4(a) Concur - It is to be noted that our request not only concerned the Roosevelt School property but also an involvement with the Cook County Forest Preserve District by way of a temporary construction easement.
In telephone conversation with Mr. Bob Frantz of the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation on November 14, 1974, Mr. Frantz said no additional response would be forthcoming concerning the Cook County Forest Preserve Property since the material submitted for early coordination and our cooperative efforts with the Forest Preserve District were well documented.
